title: BENGALURU (ISRO) - ISRO Successfully Launches Gaganyaan Test Vehicle Mission
text: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully conducted the flight test of the Gaganyaan Test Vehicle Development Flight (TV-D1) from Sriharikota. The mission demonstrated the in-flight abort system of the Crew Escape System, confirming astronaut safety parameters for upcoming human spaceflight missions.

title: WASHINGTON (NASA) - NASA James Webb Space Telescope Discovers Ancient Galaxy Cluster
text: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has captured unprecedented images of a massive galaxy cluster forming in the early universe, just 600 million years after the Big Bang. Astrophysicists confirmed peer-reviewed spectroscopic measurements published in the Astrophysical Journal.
subject: science

title: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Adjusts Interest Rates to Maintain Economic Stability
text: The Federal Reserve announced a quarter-point interest rate adjustment following its monetary policy committee meeting. Chairman Jerome Powell stated the decision aims to maintain price stability while sustaining economic growth across manufacturing and technology sectors.

title: LONDON (BBC) - UK Prime Minister Announces New Clean Energy Investment Package
text: The UK Prime Minister announced a 5 billion pound green energy infrastructure initiative aimed at accelerating offshore wind power generation and expanding grid capacity across Great Britain by 2030.

title: BENGALURU (ISRO) - Chandrayaan 3 Pragyan Rover Confirms Presence of Sulfur on Lunar Surface
text: ISRO scientists confirmed that the Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS) instrument onboard the Pragyan rover unequivocally detected sulfur on the lunar surface near the south pole, along with aluminum, calcium, iron, and titanium.

text: NASA engineers at Kennedy Space Center completed critical fueling tests for the Space Launch System rocket and Orion spacecraft ahead of the planned Artemis II manned lunar flyby mission.

text: Representatives from over 190 nations concluded two weeks of international climate negotiations by signing a binding accord to accelerate renewable energy transitions and reduce carbon emissions globally.

text: The World Health Organization issued updated global public health guidelines to strengthen early warning surveillance networks and medical supply distribution channels across member states.

text: The Bank of Japan launched the second phase of its central bank digital currency (CBDC) pilot program, testing interbank settlement efficiency and cross-border digital payment infrastructure.

text: An international archaeological expedition discovered a 3,000-year-old intact tomb near Luxor containing royal papyrus scrolls, gold statuettes, and decorated sarcophagi from the New Kingdom era.

text: Phase III clinical trial results published in the New England Journal of Medicine demonstrate that an mRNA-based personalized melanoma vaccine significantly reduced recurrence rates when combined with immunotherapy.

title: BERLIN (BBC) - Solar Cell Efficiency Record Broken by German Materials Research Lab
text: Researchers at the Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin achieved a world record 33.7 percent energy conversion efficiency for a silicon-perovskite tandem solar cell, verified by independent testing laboratories.

text: ISRO's Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV-C58) successfully deployed the X-ray Polarimeter Satellite (XPoSat) into a 650km low Earth orbit to study polarization of cosmic X-rays from black holes and neutron stars.

title: WASHINGTON (NASA) - NASA Hubble Space Telescope Detects Water Vapor on Nearby Exoplanet
text: Astronomers analyzing data from NASA's Hubble Space Telescope confirmed the presence of atmospheric water vapor on an exoplanet located in the habitable zone of a nearby red dwarf star.

text: Real Madrid won their 15th European Champions League title following a 2-0 victory at Wembley Stadium. UEFA officials praised the tournament organization and global viewership records.

text: The 2024 Summer Olympic Games officially concluded in Paris after 16 days of athletic competition featuring 10,500 athletes from 206 national committees.
